conflicts.fact: Where fertilisation happens in tilapia/fish and whether fish use internal fertilisation: Lesson 1 sorts tilapia-like and shark/guppy examples under internal fertilisation types, while Lessons 3 and 7 say fish use external fertilisation.
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 Observe Part B: tilapia-like mouthbrooder, shark/guppy sorted among oviparous/viviparous/ovoviviparous internal fertilisation examples, but Part A says tilapia spawn externally. Lesson 7: frogs and fish (external). This is internally inconsistent about fish within Lesson 1 and with later lessons' simple grouping.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the dissection/specimen was from
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 refers to 'annotated drawings from Lesson 4', but the dissection and drawings were done in Lesson 2; Lesson 4 covered hormone charts.

conflicts.fact: Frequency of hen egg-laying / hen egg release
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3: hen about one egg a day; Lesson 4: hen lays one egg every day or so; Lesson 4 overview: hen lays one egg at a time. Mostly compatible, but Lesson 2 and 4 differ on the cow: Lesson 4 says cows release one egg at a time under hormone control in the same way as humans.

Lesson 1 groups hens as oviparous and internal fertilisation; Lesson 7 states external fertilisation only for frogs and fish, hens internal. Lesson 7 lists 'external, oviparous, viviparous, ovoviviparous' as 'types of fertilisation and development', mixing fertilisation site with development type, whereas Lesson 1 separates them.
